summary.quote: For consistency with prior mirikizumab studies, the inclusion criteria [12b] is updated with the following maximum baseline liver enzyme levels: alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) ≤2 x ULN alkaline phosphatase (ALP) ≤1.5 x ULN, and total bilirubin level (TBL) ≤1.5 x ULN. To specify that any participant who experiences serious or severe GI AEs that are consistent with worsening of UC and do not improve with the recommendations for management of intolerable GI symptoms related to tirzepatide will be evaluated for UC disease worsening. To clarify that every symptom-directed examination will also include an examination of the heart, lungs, abdomen, neurological system, thyroid, and visual examination of the skin, consistent with the existing text in the schedule of activities under "Complete Physical Examination." To add acute kidney injury as an AESI to the protocol. To include pregnancy testing every 4 weeks. This can include home urine pregnancy testing. To update that follow-up information for pregnancy outcomes for participant and neonate will be collected until termination of the pregnancy or for at least 12 months post-delivery.
The overall rationale for the amendment is to update the protocol based on response provided to assessment RFIs on the EU Part I dossier.
The main reason for this amendment is to address regulatory feedback.
This amendment is considered to be substantial. The amendment is considered to be substantial because it is likely to have a significant impact on the safety or the rights of the study participants

text.quote: Must be ≥18 to ≤70 years of age at the time of signing the ICF.
Have had an established diagnosis of UC for ≥3 months before baseline (Visit 2/randomization), which includes endoscopic evidence of UC and a histopathology report that supports a diagnosis of UC.

name.quote: Type of participant and disease characteristics

text.quote: Have moderately to severely active UC as defined by an mMS of 5 to 9 points and ES of 2 to 3 (confirmed by central review) within 21 days before baseline.

name.quote: Type of participant and disease characteristics

text.quote: Are up-to date on colorectal cancer surveillance per local guidelines in case of  a family history of colorectal cancer  personal history of increased colorectal cancer risk  age >45 years,   history of UC for greater than or equal to 8 years or  other known risk factors.

Participants with a history of UC for greater than or equal to 8 years who have had a surveillance colonoscopy completed within 1 year prior to baseline must have documented negative results for colorectal dysplasia and cancer.
Are willing to consult with a dietitian or nutritionist, or equivalent qualified designee or delegate* according to local standards, to receive lifestyle management counseling during trial.

Have  [7a] obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2), or  [7b] overweight (BMI ≥27 kg/m2 to <30 kg/m2) and in the presence of at least 1 of these weight-related comorbid conditions:  o hypertension  o T2DM  o dyslipidemia  o obstructive sleep apnea, or  o cardiovascular disease.

Individuals AMAB and AFAB may participate in this trial, including both IOCBP and INOCBP.  Contraceptive use by participants should be consistent with local regulations regarding the methods of contraception for those participating in clinical studies.

name.quote: Sex assigned at birth and contraceptive/barrier requirements

text.quote: Are capable of giving signed informed consent as described in Section 10.1, which includes compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the ICF and in this protocol.

Have an inadequate response to, loss of response to, or intolerance to at least 1 of the medications described in inclusion criterion [10a] or [10b]. Documentation of dose, frequency, route of administration, and duration of the prior failed treatment is required or could be reported by the participant.
Are on a stable dose, defined as listed here, if using these medications:
Have clinically acceptable central laboratory test results at screening (retesting is allowed for hematology and chemistry), as assessed by the investigator, including

Are reliable and willing to make themselves available for the duration of the study and are willing to follow study procedures as required, including, but not limited to  colonoscopies  self-injecting intervention or injection by a caregiver, when applicable  maintaining a diary  completing patient-reported questionnaires, and  storing and taking provided study interventions as directed.
Have a current diagnosis of  Crohn's disease  IBD unclassified (formerly known as indeterminate colitis), or  primary sclerosing cholangitis.

Have had or will need bowel resection or intestinal or intra-abdominal surgery, including but not limited to  extensive colonic surgery for UC, for example, subtotal colectomy, ostomy, or ileoanal pouch  any small bowel or colonic surgery within 6 months prior to baseline (Visit 2), or  any non-intestinal intra-abdominal surgery within 3 months of baseline.
Are likely to require surgery for the treatment of UC during the study.
Have evidence of toxic megacolon or stricture or stenosis within the colon that cannot be traversed by a sigmoidoscope or colonoscope.
Have any history or current evidence of cancer of the GI tract.
Have had prior or current GI dysplasia, other than a completely removed low-grade dysplastic lesion, before the screening endoscopy.
Have any adenomatous polyp without dysplasia occurring in areas of the colon and rectum, that has not been removed.

Have a diagnosis of any of the following at screening or during the study:  cancer other than squamous cell or basal cell carcinoma of the skin (for details, see exclusion criterion [32])  any colonic adenomatous polyp with low-grade dysplasia not completely removed  any adenomatous polyp with high-grade dysplasia, or  evidence of dysplasia in nonpolypoid mucosa (indefinite for dysplasia, low-grade or high-grade dysplasia) in the GI tract.
Have a diagnosis of T1DM or insulin-treated T2DM.
Have any current or past history, or a diagnosis of proliferative diabetic retinopathy, diabetic maculopathy, or nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy that requires acute treatment.
Have a history of severe hypoglycemia and/or hypoglycemia unawareness within the 6 months prior to Visit 1 (screening).
Have a history of ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar state or coma in the last year.
Have a self-reported change in body weight greater than 5% (gain or reduction) within 3 months prior to Visit 1.

Have a prior or planned surgical treatment for obesity, such as gastric bypass (bariatric) surgery or restrictive bariatric surgery (for example, Lap-Band®), excluding liposuction or abdominoplasty if performed more than 1 year prior to Visit 1.
Have a known clinically significant gastric emptying abnormality (for example, severe gastroparesis or gastric outlet obstruction).
Have a family or personal history of medullary thyroid cancer (MTC) or multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) syndrome type 2.
Have a current or past history of chronic or acute pancreatitis.
Have acute or chronic hepatitis, or signs and symptoms of any other liver disease other than nonalcoholic fatty liver disease.
Have a diagnosis or history of malignant disease within 5 years prior to baseline (Visit 2).

Have a significant uncontrolled illness that in the opinion of the investigator may compromise the participant's safety or interfere with interpretation of data; such illnesses or conditions include, but are not limited to

Have a history of unstable major depressive disorder (MDD), suicidal ideation, or other severe psychiatric disorder (for example, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, or other serious mood or anxiety disorder) within the last 2 years.
Have a history of chronic alcohol abuse, IV drug abuse, or other illicit drug abuse within 1 year before screening colonoscopy.
Are, in the judgment of the investigator, actively suicidal and therefore deemed to be at significant risk for suicide.
Have answered "yes" to either Question 4 or Question 5 on the "Suicidal Ideation" portion of the C-SSRS and the ideation occurred within the past month.
Have had extra-abdominal surgery and have not recovered fully following surgery, including complete wound healing, before screening.

Have  a known or suspected allergy or hypersensitivity to mirikizumab or tirzepatide, any of their excipients, or any other GLP-1 receptor agonists or excipients, that would pose an unacceptable risk to the participant in this study  clinically significant multiple or severe drug allergies, or  a history of severe post-treatment hypersensitivity reactions, including, but not limited to, erythema multiforme major, linear IgA dermatosis, toxic epidermal necrolysis, or exfoliative dermatitis.

Have a current or recent acute, active infection. For at least 30 days before screening (Visit 1) and up to the randomization visit (Visit 2), participants must have no symptoms or signs of confirmed or suspected infection, and must have completed any appropriate anti-infective treatment.

Have had any of the following types of infection, including chronic or recurring extraintestinal infections, within 3 months prior to the screening visit (Visit 1) or develops any of these infections before the randomization visit (Visit 2):
Have a nonserious extraintestinal infection that is not adequately treated prior to screening and randomization.
Have active TB or untreated LTBI.
Have HIV infection.
Have a current infection with HBV; that is, positive for HBsAg and/or PCR positive for HBV DNA (Section 8.2.11).
Have a current infection with HCV; that is, positive for HCV RNA (Section 8.2.12).
Have a known active COVID-19 infection.
Have C. difficile or other intestinal infection within 30 days of screening colonoscopy or test positive at screening for C. difficile or for other intestinal pathogens.
Have a confirmed diagnosis of cytomegalovirus-associated colitis.
Have received any of the following for the treatment of UC within the timeframes listed in this table:
Have failed 4 or more classes of advanced therapies approved for the treatment of UC.
Have received any of the medications within the required washout period described in this table.
Have a previous failure or intolerance to GLP-1 receptor agonists or tirzepatide.
Are currently enrolled in any other clinical study involving an investigational product or any other type of medical research judged not to be scientifically or medically compatible with this study.

Are Lilly employees or employees of third-party organizations involved with the study.

Are investigator site personnel directly affiliated with this study and/or their immediate families. Immediate family is defined as a spouse, parent, child, or sibling, whether biological or legally adopted.

Are unwilling or unable to comply with the use of a data collection device to directly record data from the participant daily for the duration of this study or are unable to complete other study procedures.
Are unsuitable for inclusion in the study in the opinion of the investigator or sponsor for any reason that may compromise the participant's safety or confound data interpretation.
Are pregnant, or intend to become pregnant or to breastfeed during the study or within 10 weeks after receiving the last dose of the study intervention.
Have abnormal 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) that, in the opinion of the investigator or sponsor, increases the risks associated with participating in the study.
